body.text: Research verdict: no evaluated RL policy reproduces the complete task under unchanged agent criteria v1. Seven iterations trained 6,012,928 policy decisions. Iteration4 is selected for mean ordered progress in hardware-and-wrist-compliant episodes; its final selection verdict is r0032. Iteration6 seed1019 completes three tosses/catches/turns but fails final hold and wrist RMS (76.6mm>70mm). Five counterfactual final-target holds also fail and are rejected. Reconstruction r0003 is VALID with documented warnings; all iterations, curves, videos, weights and negative verdicts are preserved. Remaining gap: stable final capture/hold and reliable composition while matching the wrist. This is my simulation claim, not an official evaluation or real-world result.

Research start: 2026-11-03 03:22:24 UTC (date -u). Eight-hour operator budget; first reconstruction has a 60-minute deadline. I will reconstruct the three toss/catch events and in-hand spins, explicitly mark unobservable ball rotation, record criteria before judging a policy, then build a physically simulated right Wuji hand and train a closed-loop network using RL. No target-environment or other-agent records are used.

Task decomposition from direct video inspection: initial hold and downward wrist preparation; release around frame53, capture67; in-hand spin/regrasp through163; release164, capture178; next spin/regrasp through200; release201, capture217; final in-hand spin and hold to314. TODO: verify contact transitions and wrist pose in MANO reconstruction; learn launch/capture; learn rotation while supported; compose three launches with the instructed intervening spins. Sphere diameter anchors scale. Independent quadratic fits to segmented free flights give camera accelerations roughly (-0.08,8.54,3.87), (-0.19,8.87,3.68), (-0.23,7.87,3.08) m/s^2, so a tilted gravity direction is necessary. body.text: Simulation r0008 validated specified masses/inertia/controllers. Direct retargeted wrist replay with naive finger synergies loses the ball; a palm-up upward stroke produces ballistic rises up to0.18m but capture rebounds and lateral drift remain. Begin PPO residual RL (closed-loop network; actions22 wrist/finger synergy residuals) over a2s launch/catch curriculum,64 parallel MuJoCo environments. Base reference and kinematic interception guide exploration; only the learned network-plus-residual policy will be reported, not these analysis controllers. Next curriculum will add supported rotation and three-cycle composition.

Second PPO run changes exploration and policy smoothing only: initial Gaussian logstd-1.5 versus-0.8 and100ms residual smoothing(alpha0.2 at50Hz). Early training episodes survive about52steps versus17steps in the unsmoothed run and occasionally generate qualifying flights. This is a policy change within simulation v1, not altered physics. Both evaluated runs will be recorded with checkpoints, curves, three views and full-criteria failures or successes.

Physics diagnosis before further training: vendor URDF convex meshes create persistent palm-to-MCP-abduction housing overlaps(about1.3mm), mechanically adjacent parts separated by the two-axis MCP chain. Those joint-bearing hull contacts push ring/little fingers away from their intended targets and destabilize a seemingly settled grip. Stopped own PPO jobs with preserved checkpoints; both will be evaluated and recorded in their original simulation v1. Build simulation v2 with explicit exclusions only for these mechanical neighbor bodies, keeping all ball-hand and inter-finger collisions. No hand mass, joint limits or actuation limits change.

body.text: Reconstruction v1 r0002 and criteria v1 r0003 are recorded before simulation. Retargeting maps robot +Y to anatomical palm normal and -Z to wrist-to-middle-MCP, using a fixed translation to put the initial wrist at z=0.65 m. Robot pad-center IK replaces unreliable reconstructed finger contacts; initial ball offset in wrist coordinates is [0.008,0.052,-0.140] m, an anatomical palm-size adaptation. A residual PPO policy with deployable observations is planned. The analysis baseline has no spin primitive and its performance will be reported separately; it is not a learned policy.

body.text: Geometric rolling-IK analysis (not a policy result) loses the ball within about0.3s even with pad-focused tripod grasps and center feedback; it is rejected as a teacher. Position-PPO long-spin motion is partial, and smooth synergy PPO is stable but slow. Run5 starts from run3 weights and widens the curriculum to2.18-5.38,5.94-6.60,7.20-10s, using baseline physics snapshots without extra settling. Its directional spin reward has equal per-rad/s slope in all phases (target4,18,3rad/s), addressing the much shorter second spin; no verification threshold changes.

The original .005m torsional friction length is uncalibrated and may resist tennis-ball spin too strongly. MuJoCo documents torsion as a contact-patch length (https://mujoco.readthedocs.io/en/3.17.0/computation/). I will test .0005m nominal, with all specified mass, geometry, inertia, sliding friction and hardware unchanged, and measure sensitivity up to .005m rather than claim either is experimentally identified. This is a physics hypothesis requiring a new simulation record, not a relaxed task criterion. Pad-focused geometric IK did not solve stable rolling, so the robust original grasp remains.

body.text: Mixed training now spans toss transitions and final settling. Flight rewards track physically generated baseline paths that already meet criteria, while held-stage rewards retain the anatomical wrist/palm reference. This tests smoother exploration without any privileged observations or execution-time planning.

simulator.name: MuJoCoWarp
simulator.contact: Same MuJoCo3.17 implicitfast1kHz elliptic condim4 contact, ball priority1
simulator.friction: Ball-dominant sliding0.9, torsion0.0005m, rolling0.00002m (rolling coefficient inactive at condim4). These are explicitly inferred, not measurements.
simulator.parallelism: CUDA graph with20 one-millisecond controller/physics ticks per50Hz network command. Reference commands and rate limits updated500Hz.

scene.robot: Wuji Hand 2.2 right; all URDF inertias, link transforms, 20 joints and vendor meshes preserved; within-finger housing collision excluded; inter-finger collisions enabled
scene.object: 0.065 m diameter sphere, .0577 kg, isotropic inertia .000041 kg m2. Separate free joint. Visual stripe sites have no collision, sensing or mass effect.
scene.floor: z=0; world X forward Y left Z up

reference.retarget: +Y robot palm normal = cross(index-MCP minus wrist, little-MCP minus wrist); -Z = wrist-to-middle MCP; +X completes right handed frame. Fixed translation puts initial root at [0,0,.65]. No per-episode reference alignment. 9-frame Savitzky-Golay smoothing of wrist position.
reference.ball_adaptation: Constant world translation corresponding to local initial ball [0.008,.052,-.140] m in robot wrist frame, adapting human to robot palm dimensions. This preserves measured flight heights.
reference.fingers: Initial pad-center IK to sphere with penetration penalty, then analysis opening reference near annotated release/catch times. Exact MANO contacts are too uncertain to retarget literally.

base_controller_v2.offline_method: Differential evolution of 8 parameters per toss using MuJoCo rollouts, only during offline reference development. No planning or optimization at execution.
base_controller_v2.closed_loop_part: Time-gated horizontal correction from observed ball center to desired palm-relative center, capped to60mm per axis; gain0.46-0.90. Does not observe contacts.
base_controller_v2.untrained_baseline: Updated reference has0/10 complete successes; all spins fail. Every episode has3 captured flights, but flight ranges are reported in validation, not assumed to pass.
base_controller_v2.final_policy_plan: PPO residual fingers must learn directional spins. Baseline alone is explicitly not a learned task solution.

constant_adjustment_v6.selection: Candidate1 of40 in calibration16b, selected using frozenPPO15 and3 reference-development seeds5000-5002, not verification seeds. Constant settings; no search at execution. Second rise.211-.219m, duration.423-.427s; third rise.306-.312m, first120ms contact.85-1.00, wrist max.09782m. No full task verdict from calibration.

wrist_and_fingers.wrist: 1 kHz specified Cartesian impedance Kp=2000,Kd=60,rot Kp=20,Kd=.4, own-weight and COM moment compensation .6878*9.81, force norm<=30N torque<=2Nm; executed targets rate limited at500Hz to2.5m/s,6rad/s; free joint unconstrained workspace
wrist_and_fingers.fingers: Specified 1kHz PD gains, zero requested joint feedforward, torque clipped to individual effort limits. Joint target clipped to URDF limits and additionally rate limited to70% motor speed at500Hz. Actual position/speed checked without state clipping; violations fail verification. Armature as hand spec.
wrist_and_fingers.policy_rate: Learned network 50Hz; its outputs held for ten500Hz command ticks. Command bridge updates rate limits at500Hz and impedance/PD at1kHz.
wrist_and_fingers.noise: Deployable policy encoder readings have independent Gaussian std .002rad and .05rad/s. Controllers use true states as actuator inner-loop measurements.
wrist_and_fingers.GPU_port: World force and body-frame generalized root torque are equivalent to applying the specified wrist wrench at the root origin. Own-hand COM compensation uses subtree_com. Conservative caps29.99999N and1.999999Nm and one-ULP inward motor torque caps prevent float32 roundoff exceeding hardware maxima. No qpos/qvel clipping.
wrist_and_fingers.policy_decoder: PPO outputs20 independent joint target-velocity increments (.5 times motor max speed), integrated into position residuals, bounded1.2rad; command targets kept0.05rad within joint limits with integrator anti-windup. Original hardware PD remains unchanged. Before firstcatch+.02s and after9.85s residuals decay. Finger opening reference also decays residuals. Wrist follows disclosed basev2.

target_guard.inputs: Noisy joint encoders at500Hz: sigma q=.002rad, qd=.05rad/s; prior targets and public limits/gains/armature only. No contacts/forces/parameters observed.
target_guard.equation: tau_lo=clip(Iarm*(-vn-venc)/.002,effort); tau_hi=clip(Iarm*(vp-venc)/.002,effort). Position target projected into [qenc+(tau_lo+kd*venc)/kp, qenc+(tau_hi+kd*venc)/kp], then URDF range.
target_guard.meaning: A conservative command filter based on minimum joint inertia; actual velocity/position still measured independently and must pass exact criteria. It can command braking targets immediately; inner1kHz PD/effort clamp unchanged.
target_guard.noise: Warp stateless Gaussian stream byworld and500Hz counter, independent samples; counter persists acrosstrainingresets.

initial_conditions.reason: Initial held palm-up state adapted from reconstructed first frame; no attachment or later ball state reset.

episode.termination: Training may terminate on drop, excessive separation or hardware violation. Evaluation always records the full episode and any failure. No object forces beyond gravity/contact.

limitations: Convex link collision hulls approximate vendor geometry; no detailed felt/soft-pad deformation or air drag.
Friction is inferred. Validation distribution does not demonstrate real-hardware transfer.
Human contact reconstruction is partial, so initial finger geometry comes from robot pad IK.
Success in this smaller torsion model will not establish success at the original0.005m. Evaluate friction sensitivity separately; physical contact-patch size is not identified by the video.
GPUfloat32 contact trajectories differ from CPU by millimetres during impact; this is a distinct recorded simulation version.
Contact-patch torsion remains inferred, nominal0.0005m.
Training resets may sample physically generated catch-state snapshots; verification uses uninterrupted episodes with physical initial settling.
Command guard is not a proof against arbitrary contact impulses; every actual1kHz trajectory remains subject to exact hardware checks.

body.text: Simulation v1 baseline uses a collision-aware initial cup, measured wrist reference and disclosed 100ms launch feedforward pulses. The zero-residual controller fails: only one toss (0.150m rise), no catch, floor loss; initial support .941 and no finger hardware violations. This baseline is explicitly not a learned solution. PPO will use deployable states and residual26 actions, no contacts or parameters in observations. Dense ball trajectory, ordered contact-phase and spin rewards, with reference-state training initialization followed by complete episodes. Baseline and validation artifacts are preserved in research/sim/.

simulator.name: MuJoCo
simulator.contact: rigid mesh convex hulls; sphere ball; solref .008 1; solimp .95 .99 .001 .5 2; friction hand .9 .005 .0001, ball .8 .005 .0001, condim4 ball

scene.robot: Public Wuji Hand 2.2 right URDF masses/inertias/meshes imported by MjSpec; fixed bodies fused; all20 joints retained. Connected knuckle assemblies and links of same finger excluded from self contact because CAD overlaps. Cross-finger collisions remain.
scene.objects: Sphere radius .0325m, mass .0577kg, diagonal shell inertia .000041 kg m²; floor z0; no constraints on ball

reference.method: Palm axes from reconstructed wrist/middle MCP and index-pinky direction; filtered human joints, interpolated to500Hz, rigid translation to wrist z.65m. Object support center adapted to robot grasp; flights use measured contact timings and gravity, interpolated between retargeted release/catch centers. Finger baseline surface-distance IK cup/open pattern. Baseline launch feedforward vertical2.5m/s for100ms at each reconstructed release; policy learns residuals. Ball orientation absent from reconstruction and not imitated.

wrist_and_fingers.controller: 1kHz Cartesian impedance with specified gains 2000/60 linear,20/.4 angular, gravity compensation for hand only, force norm30N torque2Nm. Wrench applied at wrist origin with mj_applyFT. Executed wrist target at500Hz rate-limited2.5m/s and6rad/s, linear feedforward clipped2.5m/s; rotational feedforward0. Finger PD specified gains, torque clips at exact efforts, armatures from vendor .0005/.0002. No velocity projection or external impulse; actual speeds audited every1ms.
wrist_and_fingers.policy: 100Hz network residual held for five500Hz commands; reference recomputed500Hz. Finger target slew limited .65*URDF speed by policy action mapping, before specified PD, to reduce demand transients. Finger target residual .6rad*tanh, wrist position residual .10m*tanh, rotation residual .35rad*tanh. Encoder noise sigma .002rad,.05rad/s; no tactile/current sensing.

initial_conditions.reason: Reconstructed palm-up grasp adapted by collision surface distance IK to robot anatomy. Free wrist at .65m; no fixed mount, object attachment or floor support. Evaluation perturbations match criteria v1.

episode.training_termination: time limit, floor contact, ball-reference distance>.20m, non-finite state; evaluation logs complete episode even on failure

validation.baseline_result: Untrained zero residual fails: initial support .941, single flight rise .150m, no catch, ball hits floor; wrist RMS pose error 1.99deg,.00813m; no finger violations. Native batch throughput33475 decisions/s at32env16threads. This baseline is not a learned policy.

limitations: Rigid felt/shell approximation, no soft pads/deformation/air drag; contact coefficients inferred.
No real-hardware validation; sphere orientation checked in simulated material frame only.

body.text: Simulation3 r0017 adds reward-only1kHz capture continuity; four backend-equivalence episodes retain bit-identical physics/actor observations. Starting PPO iteration4 from iteration2 with lower exploration (std scale.35, caps sigma exp(-2) fingers/exp(-3) wrist), stronger hardware cost, smooth speed margin above70% limit, spin progress, launch velocity targets for.290/.330/.405m rises, and exact first100ms capture support reward. Capture reward is gated to first contact window per intended capture, preventing reward for extra micro-tosses. No physics/controller or criteria change. Iteration3 rotation variant continues independently.

Feasibility check for strict toss/catch thresholds: measured rises.285/.323/.389m imply vertical release speeds sqrt(2gh)=2.365/2.517/2.763m/s. Third toss needs about.263m/s beyond2.5m/s wrist target, compatible in scale with a40mm finger lever at6.6rad/s (below relevant joint speed limits), though coupled dynamics still matter. For capture, ball kinetic energy at2.7m/s is.210J. Following downward near2.3m/s reduces relative ball speed to.4m/s. A30N downward wrist wrench with.7455kg combined mass gives about50m/s² downward acceleration including gravity, reaching2.3m/s in46ms over53mm. This is a rough bound supporting gentle-capture feasibility, not a proof of controllability. It motivates learning anticipatory wrist descent while retaining all criteria.

body.text: At minute 10, the first complete reference passes the required format and all quality checks in aggregate (warnings retained). MoGe focal prior 1304.7 px disagrees with silhouette-and-gravity calibration 938.2 px; frame bootstrap 95% interval 923.3–1026.0 px. I will test the geometric calibration, improve occluded held-ball depth with temporal/contact consistency, and strengthen explicitly observed thumb opposition. No robot training simulation has been built. Stage 1 still ends 05:51:20Z.

Hand fitting refinement uses a workspace copy of the supplied method, generated reproducibly by research/code/make_supervised_fitter.py. Installed code is unchanged. The copy replaces the polygonal sphere distance with its exact analytic distance, checks all 778 hand vertices rather than 103 probes, and adds a weighted thumb/opposing-finger surface-contact loss only on observed held intervals 0–40,70–155,182–193,222–314. Full-default fitting and supervised unmodified baselines were already run. These changes address the recorded penetration/opposition warnings; they do not fabricate unsupported object spin.

Texture-motion diagnostics support long finger-driven turns in frames 74–155 and 225–302, with partial visible angular path estimates 6.77 and 6.28 rad. The short turn after the second catch, frames 182–193, is much smaller: partial estimate 0.66 rad across 10/11 frame pairs. These are noisy partial path lengths, not absolute orientations or net rotations. Therefore a uniform full-revolution criterion would misrepresent the demonstration; the later criteria will distinguish the long spin intervals from the brief second turn.

body.text: Version 2 camera rationale: direct known-radius spherical silhouette fits constrained by shared 9.81 m/s² gravity select focal 938.2 px; the MoGe prior is 1304.7 px (1.39x). The focal sensitivity profile and frame bootstrap (923.3–1026.0 px interval) support the shorter focal. It was selected on image/physics residuals, not hand-contact convenience. Full all-vertex validation now passes contact opposition, penetration and self-intersection. Remaining continuity warning concerns uncertain blurred prelaunch depth, being refined with hand-conditional temporal fitting.

Reference wrist feasibility calculation (no robot simulation): the calibrated MANO wrist has a peak 9.84 rad/s between native frames, while hardware executed-target rotation is limited to 6 rad/s. Its largest 0.328 rad increment requires at least 54.7 ms at that target limit, versus 33.3 ms in the clip. The later wrist comparison must disclose rate-limited retargeting and justified pose/timing tolerance; exact framewise replay is not a feasible target command. This is a calculation on the reconstruction, not evidence of robot performance.

A viewer-tool file-mode issue was found: it copies read-only static assets, so rebuilding into an existing viewer directory can fail before updating data. The first reconstruction record used its earlier default-fit viewer while its comparison video/validation used the selected contact-refined fit; version 1 viewer therefore has a small fit mismatch. Version 2 was built in a fresh directory and is consistent. Subsequent versions will use fresh viewer directories and check the command exit status before recording. Installed tools are unchanged.

Elapsed check: approximately 30/60 minutes of Stage 1, approximately 30/480 minutes of total budget. Two VALID reconstruction versions are recorded; a third selected fit is being validated. Ball translation/image agreement has improved, all observed hand frames are supported, and contact/opposition is physically checked. Remaining work in Stage 1 is sensitivity analysis, final reconstruction audit, and evidence-based threshold preparation. No training simulation or PPO training has begun.

body.text: Six-fit reconstruction sensitivity analysis is complete. Across nominal weak/strong opposition, ±2 px hand-mask boundaries and 63/67 mm diameter endpoints, relative wrist motion changes by median 11.1 mm, p95 19.4 mm, max 27.9 mm; wrist orientation changes by median 3.13°, p95 4.75°, max 6.19°. Local fingertip variation is larger: p95 24.9 mm, max 49.3 mm. Absolute camera-depth range can reach 165 mm, while relative motion is more stable. Therefore later training should use ball/wrist motion as stronger reference evidence and avoid treating fitted fingertips as exact targets. A swept-sphere blur sensitivity model selected effectively zero interval; that rejects this binary-union approximation, not actual optical blur. No robot training simulation has been built.

body.text: At approximately 57 minutes, five VALID reference versions have been recorded. The selected version 5 passes all required checks with explicit focal-prior and one prelaunch continuity warning; no incomplete/failed check is hidden. All provenance inputs match current archived files. Final handoff basis is orthonormal (max error 6.7e-16, determinant 1) and +X points toward the thumb/index side in every frame, matching Wuji right-hand axis semantics. Rotation remains unobservable. The full 60-minute reconstruction gate is still in force; criteria, robot simulation and training have not begun.

Stage 1 is complete after the full 60-minute gate (start 04:51:20Z, boundary 05:51:20Z). Selected reconstruction is version 5, record r0014: VALID with all checks evaluated, no quality failures, and explicitly documented continuity/focal warnings. Five reference versions and their refinements remain in the append-only record. No robot training simulation or PPO policy was built before the gate. Next: record criteria, then build the training simulation. Hard deadline remains 12:51:20Z.

Initial robot grasp validation retained the ball, and the wrist showed the expected 0.283 mm object-weight offset, but finger speeds violated hardware limits. Diagnosis: geometric fitting forced the robot pinky/ring into 2–5 mm self-intersections. Contact impulses caused the speed spikes; motor torque saturation itself remained correct. I will add robot self-collision distance constraints and weaken the unnecessary all-five-fingertip target. This is simulation/initial-state validation, not PPO training, and no violating policy will be reported.

body.text: The first two PPO runs each completed 1,507,328 environment transitions. Fixed seeds 0–2 fail all full-task trials at the first catch, with no hardware violations. Isolated reference-reset turns show iteration 1 angular paths 5.05/5.67 rad but excursions 1.50/1.65 rad and contact gaps 34/16 ms; iteration 2 paths 1.73/3.76 rad and excursions 0.43/1.28 rad. Thus path alone overstates useful rotation. Next: separate throw/catch curriculum and an excursion-aware held-turn reward. Criteria v1 stay unchanged. Baseline zero-residual control also fails all three full trials.

body.text: For a second throw curriculum, replace the reward-only human ball path by a ballistic arc between robot grasp centers at the measured release/catch times. Keep the selected reconstruction wrist poses and the recorded verification criteria unchanged. This addresses human-to-robot fingertip reach mismatch, not a relaxation of the toss test. The actual ball remains a free body with only collision/gravity forces; the arc is only a training reward target. Separate excursion-aware turning PPO and original-target throwing PPO continue for comparison. Higher hardware terminal penalties are used in the new curricula.

Run offline CEM only to study a partial first-throw reference: finger opening/closing targets and timing, small wrist translation bump, and catch translation. This is analysis/reference building, not an RL stage, teacher, or online planner. It does not spin the ball or execute the ordered task. If a resulting reference is used, publish its standalone performance and retain a deployable PPO residual for the reported policy.

The MANO fingertip-displacement reference is not a solution: isolated first-turn baseline has 3.76 rad angular path but only 0.73 rad excursion; second-turn reference loses retention (0.776, gap 224 ms). Both have no hardware violation in this test. This supports using reconstruction as a guide rather than treating collision-constrained IK as successful execution. Retain the original learned turn curriculum while testing whether a smaller reference contribution can help.

Six improved VALID versions were recorded, ending with geometric focal estimation and a scene-wide hand refit; all315 frames and required artifacts/checks are present. Version6 is the skill reference. Remaining limitations are three rapid-launch continuity warnings, monocular depth/camera assumptions and unobservable global ball orientation. No training simulation or policy was built during the first hour. I am now recording strict measurement-based own criteria before simulation construction; the eight-hour deadline remains15:54:27Z.

Simulation validation found a real retargeting failure: fingertip-only inverse kinematics placed robot ring/pinky links in8mm interpenetration, causing contact impulses above finger speed limits and ejecting the ball during the initial hold. This is not a learned-policy failure and training has not started. I am adding cross-finger collision penalties and moderate abduction priors to the offline retargeting, and excluding only nearby same-assembly CAD joint housings where convex meshes fill mechanical cutouts. Robot masses, geometry, joint limits and controller gains remain from specifications. The settled initial grasp must be physical and hardware-compliant before recording the simulation.

body.text:
Stopped on the required passing condition: verification r0105, iteration r0103, criteria1 unchanged, simulation12, immutable iter20/checkpoint_n11004928.zip.18/20 full native float64 episodes pass, zero hardware violations across20; seed1000 fails brief opposed loaded support0.79452<0.80, seed1019 third rise0.249676m<0.250m. Start2026-11-04T07:54:27Z; passing record received2026-11-04T14:08:54.886428Z, about6h14m28s. All training stopped after observing this record. The later interrupted final.zip is unverified and is not the selected policy.

Reconstruction6 was VALID after the full first-hour stage; fixed criteria1 were recorded before simulation/training. PPO-only residual learning,1024parallel physical worlds, empirical physical-prefix curricula, phase-relative allowed-state goals, separate learned toss/spin/hold heads and learned wrist feed-forward velocity were effective. Direct continuous-flight height/horizontal shaping,500Hzreward contact monitoring,and a wrist-position-error barrier corrected earlier carry/height/capture failures. Composing PPO-trained first-toss and remaining experts then further PPO fine-tuning improved the full sequence. Baseline7alone remains0/20full; no scripted spin or ball force/attachment/pose override solves the skill. The selected checkpoint collected11,004,928new transitions after earlier PPO training, not11Mtotal historical samples.

Failures and corrections remain recorded: wrapper curriculum propagation bug, earlier hardware-summary error, anatomical prefix/support bookkeeping, contact aliasing and GPU contact numerical sensitivity. Reward12 force-mask extraction logic matched native forces, but its iter21/22 GPU integrations failed initialization because the Warp Data force field was accessed as Data.efc_force. Those branches performed zero PPO updates; they are NOT responsible for the passing policy, which uses reward11. They were not repaired after the stopping condition was met.

Evidence includes all20metrics, raw succe…

The skill consists of two sequential side grasps, in-hand quarter-turns and leftward placements, white before black. I will use observed plug motion and a scene-conditioned MANO fit as the reference, explicitly flag hidden poses, then train a closed-loop residual RL policy with wrist similarity and physical grasp/placement rewards. Stage 1 started at approximately 21:54 UTC with a 60-minute deadline.

Camera focal length is not identifiable from the rounded plug corner annotations: focal profiling changes reprojection RMS only weakly. I use the MoGe focal as an explicitly inferred prior and known plug dimensions for metric scale. I rejected unstable sparse plane-homography translation and estimate horizontal camera drift from the stationary plugs with fixed optical height.

The initial hand fit passed silhouette/contact-distance checks but failed physical grasp reconstruction: thumb contact fraction was zero and finger self-intersections occurred in 51.7% of valid frames. Explicit thumb/opposing-finger constraints raised opposed-grasp fractions to 89.1% (white) and 96.2% (black), with self-intersections reduced to 35.5%. I am adding a bone-capsule separation prior and will retain the independent validator findings, including any remaining failures.

body.summary: VALID reference contract, overall quality pass with disclosed contact/collision warnings. Two sequential right-hand charger pickups, in-hand turns and leftward upright placements. Monocular camera prior, specified metric geometry, 436-frame object references and 360-frame MANO hand fit.

components.method: Specified geometry with per-frame segmented silhouette fits, support constraints and marked occlusion
components.note: 436 white image-supported estimates and 354 black estimates; in-hand depth/rotation uncertain. Median visible-scene IoU 0.8204/0.8006.

components.method: HaWoR plus scene-conditioned MANO fit with thumb/opposing contacts and capsule separation
components.note: 360 valid right-hand frames; two brief finger-intersection frames and a 6.92 mm black contact penetration remain.

components.method: Visual contact-phase annotation, independently checked geometric opposition
components.note: White 78–215, black 279–385; boundaries about 5 frames uncertain; opposition 97.1%/100%.

components.note: Visual rounded edges and USB recess omitted; rest stability displacement below 0.5 mm.

Finger mesh intersections in frames 279 and 314; 6.92 mm black hand-object penetration in frame 336; these are reference uncertainties, not permitted robot dynamics.

reprojection.note: against your own masks: agreement with them is necessary, not sufficient (3D errors along the viewing ray are invisible here)

anatomical_contact.note: a grasp needs the thumb and an opposing finger on opposite sides of the object; single-finger pushes or palm support are legitimate but must be stated in the analysis. Low penetration does not imply contact.

penetration_hand_object.note: unsigned (lower bound) distances where the object mesh is not watertight

self_penetration.note: triangle intersections between different fingers (FCL); counts are not volumes

physics.note: free-flight intervals are given with --flight OBJ=a:b; rest intervals default to object intervals without contact

handedness_scale.note: left/right are the demonstrator's anatomical hands; a hand is never mirrored

camera_focal.note: MoGe intrinsics are a learned prior; the focal should be calibrated against known geometry (camera_calib.py pnp). A large disagreement needs its explanation in NOTES.md (which one is wrong, and why).

body.text: I will use closed-loop residual PPO on retargeted wrist/finger references. LEARNING.md explicitly permits residual RL above a reference/base controller. The final actor will be a neural network updated from simulator rewards, evaluated with its learned residual active; no direct object forces, attachments or pose overwrites will assist manipulation. References and offline kinematic fitting are initialization/reward support, not the reported policy. Sources: PPO (arxiv.org/abs/1707.06347) and Residual RL for Robot Control (arxiv.org/abs/1812.03201).

Start time (date -u): 2026-11-03T03:22:26Z. Eight-hour operator budget; Stage 1 reconstruction deadline 2026-11-03T04:22:26Z. Read task, scene/object specifications, hardware specification, and demo2sim documents. Task: sequentially pick white then black charger from table right, lift and reorient blades-up, move left, release upright. Reconstruction precedes building the training simulation. All results are my own simulation claims.

Reconstruction analysis: white-first then black; supporting table; right hand only. SAM3 masks and known-geometry PyTorch3D pose fitting, HaWoR initialization plus required MANO fitting. Unseeded white fitting reversed blade direction at high IoU; local tracker copy now accepts a PnP initialization. Focal profile is weak (rounded corners and dimension uncertainty); chose 1060 px consistent with MoGe priors 1074/1045 px. Estimated camera motion from background rotation and the passive charger. Rest support is constrained, and hidden/lost object frames stay invalid. Task decomposition is saved in research/TASK_UNDERSTANDING.md.

Re-read updated README stopping rule after operator update. Hard deadline 2026-11-03T11:22Z. Reserve final minutes for a best-policy verification and reflection if no pass occurs earlier. The default MANO fit gave hand-mask IoU 0.829 but only 0.418 contact coverage, indicating a monocular depth mismatch; testing documented fitting settings with larger contact capture radius, fixed scale, and stronger contact/penetration/depth-order terms. No training simulation has been built.

Independent reference checks exposed two errors hidden by the fitter summary: thumb contact was absent (closest middle/ring probes satisfied the loss), and distal fingers intersected in about 30% of valid frames. Support enforcement by vertical shifts also damaged image agreement. Corrected support along camera rays, preserving image centers (frame-0 IoU now 0.838 white/0.892 black). Testing a documented local copy of the required MANO fitter with explicit opposed thumb/finger surface contact and distal-finger separation penalties. The installed tools remain unchanged; these checks are not waived.

Planned learning approach (not yet building the training simulation): a reconstruction-derived wrist/finger reference plus a closed-loop neural residual trained by PPO. This is explicitly permitted by LEARNING.md; scripted replay is a baseline only. The policy will observe noisy encoders, wrist state, object pose estimates and phase, and supply action corrections through the specified impedance/PD controllers. Objects remain passive contact-driven rigid bodies. I will compare a zero-residual ablation and keep task, wrist and hardware metrics separate. Primary methods: https://arxiv.org/abs/1707.06347 (PPO), https://arxiv.org/abs/1812.03201 (residual RL), https://arxiv.org/abs/2106.08050 (residual RL from demonstrations). MuJoCo model semantics: https://mujoco.readthedocs.io/en/latest/XMLreference.html .

Research start: 2026-11-03T06:26:10Z (date -u). Hard deadline 2026-11-03T14:26:10Z. Reconstruct the video and validate or document an exception within the Stage 1 60-minute budget before recording criteria and building the training simulation. Task: white then black charger, each picked up from right, reoriented with blades up, carried left and released upright; use observed wrist pose as reference. All success claims will be my own simulation criteria and evidence.

Reference reconstruction in progress (start 06:26:10Z; Stage 1 deadline 07:26:10Z). Scene decomposition written after inspection of sampled and event frames. SAM3 segmentation and HaWoR initialization completed. Raw object trackers: median IoU white 0.924, black 0.868, but black blade-axis ambiguity after turning and camera drift made raw 3D motion physically inconsistent. Rejected accumulated background rotation (18 degrees drift) and ill-conditioned homography translation (>1 m). Retain fixed gravity-normal rotation prior, infer smoothed camera translation from passive plugs, and enforce a shared tabletop for observed side/upright rest phases. Constrained silhouette IoU approximately 0.852 white, 0.860 black; hidden turn frames explicitly invalid. Preliminary 2-second MuJoCo rest check drift <0.04 mm. Provided unchanged MANO fitting now runs against this scene. Main remaining reconstruction risks: precise depth, hidden grasp contacts, intersection and hand scale.

The unchanged MANO fitter has only nearest-hand-point contact, so it can satisfy contact by a middle finger while the thumb floats 65–90 mm away. It also has no finger self-collision loss. A contact-weight refit restores proximity but still fails self-intersection (20.2% of valid frames). Testing an explicitly documented local copy with an opposing thumb/distal-finger term and distal capsule separation; installed code remains unchanged. Format checker reports VALID with absolute paths, but the current geometric validation fails self-intersection; I will not call that a valid reconstruction. Stage 1 time remaining approximately 35 minutes.

Reconstruction elapsed ~31 minutes. Explicit thumb/finger contact in a local fitter copy passes anatomical-contact validation (opposed grasp fraction 0.867 white, 1.0 black) and proximity (median minimum distance 2.35/0.73 mm). It still fails self-intersection, mainly middle/ring in approach/withdrawal. Testing larger distal capsule margins and stronger silhouette fitting; separate floating-scale experiment tests the fixed-scale assumption. Known limits: white object is heavily occluded, many hand frames fail mask IoU after enforcing contact, and inferred depth needs a 25 mm uncertainty. Verification draft is written from demonstration measurements but no policy has been judged or simulation built.

Start time (date -u): 2026-11-04T03:45:00Z. Hard stop: 2026-11-04T11:45:00Z. I will reconstruct the single right-hand demonstration, record validation and limitations, define independent simulation verification criteria, build a physically actuated Wuji Hand 2.2 simulation, and train deployable closed-loop PPO policies. Reconstruction has its own 60-minute budget; incomplete or failed components will be recorded as an exception, never described as VALID.

Elapsed about 11 minutes of 8 hours. Initial silhouette tracking gave implausible charger orientations and large depth drift at rest. I replaced it with support-constrained fitting and a shared camera estimated from background rotation plus resting-object anchors. Object-only median silhouette IoU is now 0.870 white and 0.784 black; unsupported hidden poses remain invalid. Hypothesis: a demonstration-derived wrist/fingertip reference with a deployable PPO residual can bridge hand morphology while preserving the observed palm-down approach and wrist reorientation. Baseline performance must be measured separately; no scripted baseline will be reported as a learned solution.

The reconstruction currently passes check_reference.py format validation, but independent validation fails finger self-intersection (48.9% of valid frames), and opposing-thumb contact is weak (10.2% white, 8.2% black). I will not describe this as a successful quality reconstruction. The provided default MANO fit has no self-collision or mandatory opposing-finger loss, so I copied it into research/handlib_extended and added distal-finger capsule separation plus explicit thumb/opposing-finger surface-distance losses. Installed tools and hardware/object specifications remain unchanged. I will validate the modified fit and disclose its effect on silhouette agreement and anatomical contacts. PPO reference: Schulman et al., https://arxiv.org/abs/1707.06347; planned RL uses only its clipped-surrogate PPO family.

body.text: Stage 1 refinement diagnoses a capped-contact optimization failure: the default MANO fit is >7 cm from objects, beyond its 4 cm contact cap. A standard-fitter configuration with 25 cm cap, stronger contact and weaker scale prior reduces contact loss from 11.57 to .0017 and estimates hand scale1.124. I am testing a workspace copy of handlib/fit.py with distal-finger capsule repulsion and explicit thumb/opposing-surface contact terms to reduce the baseline finger intersections. Installed tools are unchanged; code/config hashes and deviations will be recorded.

At 05:12 UTC, 21 minutes into Stage1, all required baseline artifacts are recorded as reconstruction version1 with explicit failed quality checks. A geometric diagnosis of the failing base: the white upright reference differs from the initial grasp by a nearly180degree turn of the local blade-gap Y axis, even though the specified rectangular body, identical blade pair and centered USB recess are invariant under180degrees about local Z. Forcing fixed labeled Y-side pads along that ambiguous symmetry branch drives white wrist IK49–54degrees from the measured wrist. I will test the symmetry-equivalent upright object goal (same geometry and blade-up task), retaining the original recorded wrist and every criterion unchanged. body.text: Research start UTC (date -u): 2026-11-04T07:54:28Z. Hard stop: 2026-11-04T15:54:28Z. Stage 1 reconstruction deadline: 2026-11-04T08:54:28Z; no training simulation will be built before it. Objective: sequential white then black plug pickup from right, upright placement on left, with demonstrator-like wrist motion. I will use only this task bundle and my own outputs; criteria and verdicts will be my own simulation claims. Learning rule: all reinforcement learning will use PPO and the reported policy will use permitted deployable observations.

Start time (date -u): 2026-11-04T19:25:03Z. Experiment D2S-PLUG-7. Hard deadline 2026-11-05T03:25:03Z. Stage 1 reconstruction will last at least until 2026-11-04T20:25:03Z before any training simulation is built. Initial understanding: sequentially grasp white then black charger from the right, lift and reorient each with blades upward, transport left, release upright and withdraw. I will quantify observed phases, poses, contacts and uncertainties from this demonstration, record the reconstruction and strict evidence-based criteria, then build physics and train a deployable closed-loop PPO policy. No prior-run records will be consulted.

Reconstruction minute 5: all 436 frames segmented; HaWoR detects right hand on frames 37–396 (360 frames). Frame-0 SAM3 masks agree visually with both chargers. Camera geometry is ill-conditioned: unconstrained rounded-corner PnP fits f=391px (RMS4.57px), whereas the MoGe prior across three frames is 1036–1074px; a combined geometric/prior estimate is 931px. Absolute background homography decomposition produced implausible camera translations up to 0.62m and is rejected. I am replacing it with sequential background rotation estimation, labeling unestimated camera translation as a limitation. Object silhouette tracks are running independently, then will be reconciled with the common tabletop and contact phases.

Reconstruction minute 15: raw silhouette tracking gives high overlap but permits physically inconsistent depths and a wrong white-plug blade orientation. A common support-height search with explicit side-lying and blade-up endpoints reaches mean endpoint IoU 0.857 and resting objects drift only 0.004mm in 1s of gravity simulation. Default MANO fitting yields mask IoU 0.8274 and contact-within-10mm share 0.861; stronger contact/penetration terms with fixed scale preserve IoU 0.8273 and reach contact share 1.0 (max penetration 0.5mm by the fit scorer). Whole-scene anatomical, intersection and continuity validation is still pending. A separate camera-translation proposal inferred from the stationary charger gives only 27mm maximum horizontal motion, unlike the rejected homography estimate; it will be checked before adoption.

body.text: At reconstruction minute28, explicit physical constraints improve opposed-grasp support to100% of evaluated contact frames for both plugs and reduce whole-scene object penetration to0.47mm white/1.36mm black. Finger self-intersection falls from58.9% to15%, but still fails. Supported hand frames fall to294 because the unchanged image-support rule rejects poor fits; mean mask IoU is0.698. A mesh audit shows prior capsule radii were too small:95th-percentile skin-to-distal-centerline distances are14.7mm thumb,11.6 index,10.5 middle,10.7 ring and10.0 little. reference.retargeting: Three physical fingertip contacts: thumb body+/-Y face15mm toward USB end; index opposing face20mm toward blades; middle opposing face5mm toward USB. Exact convex self-collision, table/object penalties. Object path/blade axis from reconstruction5, axial roll adapted as sim4. Vertical approach and2mm pad compression apply to all3 fingers. Other joint targets retain optimized poses. Two-contact full-pad-orientation alternative was tested and rejected for larger IK errors; not used.

alignment.definition: Translate reconstruction so table z=0 and initial object mean x=.1m; +Y remains left. The+50mm Y shift puts both initial centers right and both final centers left; no per-episode evaluation alignment is fitted.

wrist.type: Unconstrained6DoF free joint; no workspace box or pose constraint.
wrist.controller: 1kHz Cartesian impedance, Kp_lin2000,Kd_lin60,Kp_rot20,Kd_rot0.4; own-hand gravity and COM moment compensation; force norm30N, torque norm2Nm. Executed pose targets updated500Hz with2.5m/s and6rad/s rate limits and matching finite-difference feedforward.
wrist.software_governor: Same encoder-only500Hz target-speed governor as sim6; hardware impedance and2.5m/s,6rad/s maximum unchanged.

fingers.controller: Exact hardware joint-specific PD at1kHz; torque saturated at each published effort.20 position commands clipped to limits at500Hz; zero optional velocity targets.
fingers.armature: Vendor table:5e-4 for thumbCMC and four MCPflex,2e-4 others.
fingers.speed_rules: Actual q/qd/applied torque checked every1ms, including contact-backdriven motion. A violating trial terminates; no qvel-state clipping is used.
fingers.target_shaper: 500Hz software encoder-based brake before unchanged1kHz hardware PD: after3rad/s ordinary target slew, b=clip((abs(qd_noisy)/vmax-.45)/.20,0,1); q_target=clip((1-b)*q_target+b*(q_noisy-.12sign(qd_noisy)),URDF limits). Position noise.002rad, velocity noise.05rad/s; no contact/force input. Actual qvel is never clipped. Normal motion: nominal PD demand from noisy encoders is bounded through position-target error to15% of effort for long MCPflex and40% elsewhere. This changes software targets; hardware effort/PD gains remain exact. The full emergency brake overrides this gentle bound. Ring/pinky neural residual amplitude.03rad, first12 joints.35rad.

reward_terms.formula: Active:0.6 positional opposition else0.1 any hand;0.8 balanced force/0.6N with opposed normals;0.4exp(-pad-bodySDF^2/.02^2) each thumb/index/middle. Before supported upright left, add0.8*clip(min(three normal forces)/.3N)*clip(norm(cross(index-thumb,middle-thumb))/.0004m2), with opposition and three contacts. Once supported upright left, replace accumulated contact term by0.15*term-0.6*sum(three normal forces)+0.4 anyhand before release-due or-0.4 anyhand after. Always subtract0.15sum min(10,relu(force-4N)). Supported-before-release-due: add max_over_thumb,index,middle exp(-((bodySDF(padskin)-.0015)/.01)^2) to encourage gentle last contact. wrist.type: Unconstrained6DoF free joint; no workspace box or pose constraint.
wrist.controller: 1kHz Cartesian impedance, Kp_lin2000,Kd_lin60,Kp_rot20,Kd_rot0.4; own-hand gravity and COM moment compensation; force norm30N, torque norm2Nm. Executed pose targets updated500Hz with2.5m/s and6rad/s rate limits and matching finite-difference feedforward.
wrist.software_governor: Same encoder-only500Hz target-speed governor as sim6; hardware impedance and2.5m/s,6rad/s maximum unchanged.

fingers.controller: Exact hardware joint-specific PD at1kHz; torque saturated at each published effort.20 position commands clipped to limits at500Hz; zero optional velocity targets.
fingers.armature: Vendor table:5e-4 for thumbCMC and four MCPflex,2e-4 others.
fingers.speed_rules: Actual q/qd/applied torque checked every1ms, including contact-backdriven motion. A violating trial terminates; no qvel-state clipping is used.
fingers.target_shaper: 500Hz software encoder-based brake before unchanged1kHz hardware PD: after3rad/s ordinary target slew, b=clip((abs(qd_noisy)/vmax-.45)/.20,0,1); q_target=clip((1-b)*q_target+b*(q_noisy-.12sign(qd_noisy)),URDF limits). Position noise.002rad, velocity noise.05rad/s; no contact/force input. Actual qvel is never clipped. Normal motion: nominal PD demand from noisy encoders is bounded through position-target error to15% of effort for long MCPflex and40% elsewhere. This changes software targets; hardware effort/PD gains remain exact. The full emergency brake overrides this gentle bound. Ring/pinky neural residual amplitude.03rad, first12 joints.35rad. For phase>=240 and first12 joints only, nominal demand allowance becomes25% effort for index/middleMCPflex and60% for other first12 joints. Ring/pinky and all white-phase controls exactly sim7. This changes software position-target bounds only; full hardware gains/efforts/brakes unchanged.

body.text: BCfit reached roughly6mrad mean held-out finger-target error. Early direct-targetPPO returns became extremely negative despite hardware failures declining. Code diagnosis: wristYsequencing correction usedcurrentWristY when a lost object stayed left, allowing target drift away on repeatedcalls; unbounded wristtrackingquadratics then dominate reward. New14 will limit this correction to50mm relative to the uncorrected target and activate it only while object-wrist distance<220mm, and cap each wrist penalty at4 perstep. These are software/reward corrections, not hardware/workspace constraints or criteria changes. RestartPPO from retained BCinitialization rather than reuse this unstable continuation; record13failure evidence.

reward_terms.formula: White phases<240:1.5exp(-position_error²/.055²)+1.5exp(-SO3_error²/.45²)-8(relu(position_error-.055)/.03)²-4(relu(SO3_error-.70)/.3)². Black:original8/10 .45Gaussian each and3/2 soft penalties beyond.08m/60deg. Against unchanged raw human mount trajectory.

reward_terms.name: opposed_contact
reward_terms.formula: Active:0.6 positional opposition else0.1 any hand;0.8 balanced force/0.6N with opposed normals;0.4exp(-pad-bodySDF^2/.02^2) each thumb/index/middle. Before supported upright left, add0.8*clip(min(three normal forces)/.3N)*clip(norm(cross(index-thumb,middle-thumb))/.0004m2), with opposition and three contacts. Once supported upright left, replace accumulated contact term by0.15*term-0.6*sum(three normal forces)+0.4 anyhand before release-due or-0.4 anyhand after. Always subtract0.15sum min(10,relu(force-4N)). Supported-before-release-due: add max_over_thumb,index,middle exp(-((bodySDF(padskin)-.0015)/.01)^2) to encourage gentle last contact. Release-ready additionally needs phase>=205 white or>=373 black. Release-due requires phase>=205white/373black and span>=3.6white/3.3black, without upper bound. Actual settled/milestone/terminal eligibility retains upper duration bounds through release-ready.

reward_terms.name: lift_height
reward_terms.formula: Active phase100<=f<155white or280<=f<360black:2clip(bottom/(.015white,.035black),0,1)*(.3+.7exp(-tilt²/.45²)); after interval if left:exp(-bottom²/.005²)exp(-tilt²/.3²).

reward_terms.name: settled

reward_terms.name: milestones
reward_terms.formula: First settled/release-ready+8; first bottom>1cm+2; one-off-20 for first supporting table contact on right after an upright-air sample. One-off-20 if bottom>5mm or rotation from actual initial orientation>10deg before100ms stable opposed grasp during active phase; stable grasp flag latches once achieved.

reference.retargeting: Three physical fingertip contacts: thumb body+/-Y face15mm toward USB end; index opposing face20mm toward blades; middle opposing face5mm toward USB. Exact convex self-collision, table/object penalties. Object path/blade axis from reconstruction5, axial roll adapted as sim4. Vertical approach and2mm pad compression apply to all3 fingers. Other joint targets retain optimized poses. Two-contact full-pad-orientation alternative was tested and rejected for larger IK errors; not used.

Originalthree-contact kinematic reference has known object overlaps up to about10mm; it is a target only, actual physical rollouts and1kHz penetrationcriterion decide validity. Human/objectreconstruction5 and fixed scene alignment unchanged.

wrist.type: Unconstrained6DoF free joint; no workspace box or pose constraint.
wrist.controller: 1kHz Cartesian impedance, Kp_lin2000,Kd_lin60,Kp_rot20,Kd_rot0.4; own-hand gravity and COM moment compensation; force norm30N, torque norm2Nm. Executed pose targets updated500Hz with2.5m/s and6rad/s rate limits and matching finite-difference feedforward.
wrist.software_governor: Same encoder-only500Hz target-speed governor as sim6; hardware impedance and2.5m/s,6rad/s maximum unchanged.

fingers.controller: Exact hardware joint-specific PD at1kHz; torque saturated at each published effort.20 position commands clipped to limits at500Hz; zero optional velocity targets.
fingers.armature: Vendor table:5e-4 for thumbCMC and four MCPflex,2e-4 others.
fingers.speed_rules: Actual q/qd/applied torque checked every1ms, including contact-backdriven motion. A violating trial terminates; no qvel-state clipping is used.
fingers.target_shaper: 500Hz software encoder-based brake before unchanged1kHz hardware PD: after3rad/s ordinary target slew, b=clip((abs(qd_noisy)/vmax-.45)/.20,0,1); q_target=clip((1-b)*q_target+b*(q_noisy-.12sign(qd_noisy)),URDF limits). Position noise.002rad, velocity noise.05rad/s; no contact/force input. Actual qvel is never clipped. Normal motion: nominal PD demand from noisy encoders is bounded through position-target error to15% of effort for long MCPflex and40% elsewhere. This changes software targets; hardware effort/PD gains remain exact. The full emergency brake overrides this gentle bound. Ring/pinky neural residual amplitude.03rad, first12 joints.35rad.

scene.robot: Wuji Hand2.2 right, exact URDF links/inertias/masses and20 named joints;33 frames,27 mass-bearing links; total0.6878kg.
scene.objects: Exact provided body dimensions, blades, masses and2mm COM offsets; beveled Blender visual bodies and sharp box collision bodies/blades. Box-estimated inertia; inferred friction.
scene.collision_filter: Vendor fixed-link/neighbor overlaps excluded for URDF graph distance<=2; other physical hand contacts retained.

reference.retargeting: Three physical fingertip contacts: thumb body+/-Y face15mm toward USB end; index opposing face20mm toward blades; middle opposing face5mm toward USB. Exact convex self-collision, table/object penalties. Object path/blade axis from reconstruction5, axial roll adapted as sim4. Vertical approach and2mm pad compression apply to all3 fingers. Other joint targets retain optimized poses. Two-contact full-pad-orientation alternative was tested and rejected for larger IK errors; not used.

alignment.definition: Translate reconstruction so table z=0 and initial object mean x=.1m; +Y remains left. The+50mm Y shift puts both initial centers right and both final centers left; no per-episode evaluation alignment is fitted.

reference.runtime_use: Restored exact7bank, not11-14retarget. Referenceq plus learned residuals for all fingers. Originalthree-contact kinematic reference has known object overlaps up to about10mm; it is a target only, actual physical rollouts and1kHz penetrationcriterion decide validity. Human/objectreconstruction5 and fixed scene alignment unchanged.

wrist.type: Unconstrained6DoF free joint; no workspace box or pose constraint.
wrist.controller: 1kHz Cartesian impedance, Kp_lin2000,Kd_lin60,Kp_rot20,Kd_rot0.4; own-hand gravity and COM moment compensation; force norm30N, torque norm2Nm. Executed pose targets updated500Hz with2.5m/s and6rad/s rate limits and matching finite-difference feedforward.
wrist.software_governor: Same encoder-only500Hz target-speed governor as sim6; hardware impedance and2.5m/s,6rad/s maximum unchanged.

fingers.controller: Exact hardware joint-specific PD at1kHz; torque saturated at each published effort.20 position commands clipped to limits at500Hz; zero optional velocity targets.

fingers.speed_rules: Actual q/qd/applied torque checked every1ms, including contact-backdriven motion. A violating trial terminates; no qvel-state clipping is used.

reward_terms.name: opposed_contact
reward_terms.formula: Active:0.6 positional opposition else0.1 any hand;0.8 balanced force/0.6N with opposed normals;0.4exp(-pad-bodySDF^2/.02^2) each thumb/index/middle. Before supported upright left, add0.8*clip(min(three normal forces)/.3N)*clip(norm(cross(index-thumb,middle-thumb))/.0004m2), with opposition and three contacts. Always subtract0.15sum min(10,relu(force-4N)). Supported-before-release-due: add max_over_thumb,index,middle exp(-((bodySDF(padskin)-.0015)/.01)^2) to encourage gentle last contact. Release-ready additionally needs phase>=205 white or>=373 black. Release-due requires phase>=205white/373black and span>=3.6white/3.3black, without upper bound. Actual settled/milestone/terminal eligibility retains upper duration bounds through release-ready.

reward_terms.name: settled

reward_terms.name: milestones

Before supported upright left, add0.8*clip(min(three normal forces)/.3N)*clip(norm(cross(index-thumb,middle-thumb))/.0004m2), with opposition and three contacts. body.text:
Final reflection for the extended04:15UTC deadline. Originalstart2026-11-04T19:25:03UTC; provider shutdown killed all processes, so I recovered from retained checkpoints and recorded lost uncheckpointed steps. All new PPO training ended before04:10; the last24experiment was explicitly a zero-update transfer of already PPO-trained experts.

Final own-simulation verification r0162 is FAIL:0/20 full-criteria successes under unchanged criteria1. The selected16prefix reproduces both final upright/settled chargers20/20, all black manipulation checks20/20, hardware and [redacted]s20/20. Eighteen trials meet all criteria except wrist; one white crossing and one white-preservation case also fail. Median trial wrist positionp95 is129.4mm against100mm, and median trial rotation median26.4deg against25deg. A fresh1kHz20-case rerun reproduced every physical state exactly. This is no official evaluation and no real-hardware success.

What worked: VALID reconstruction5 after the full60-minute stage; exact hardware PD/limits with encoder-only target governors; learned PPO grasp/turn experts; frozen expert branches and reduced learning rate to prevent catastrophic forgetting; physical1kHz contact/event audits. The zero-output reference controls never solved the full task. Simple final-standing rewards produced strong partial manipulation but did not establish the demonstrated skill.

What failed: static demonstration BC did not yield full-start grasps; later stronger grip and clearance feedback produced penetration/hardware failures or wrong placement order. White approach retiming improved wrist approach, but black table-assisted turning still differs from human motion. Horizontal reference changes reduced some position errors while degrading grasp robustness. I retained the stronger measured checkpoint instead of relaxing criteria or claiming that standing alone passed.

Next I would distill physical rollouts from the successful PPO grasp experts into a wrist-constrained contact…

Operator extension recorded before resuming research. New continuation starts2026-11-05T06:24:56Z and has a NEW HARD DEADLINE2026-11-05T14:24:56Z, superseding all prior expired deadlines. Training cutoff14:14:56UTC reserves10minutes for final verification/reflection and job shutdown. Persisted research_clock.json and research_state.json updated; prior clock/result preserved. Retain VALID reconstruction5/r0012 and unchanged criteria1; do not restart reconstruction or relax criteria. Retain best16prefix checkpoint (r0117/r0118, finalrepeat r0162), with0/20strictsuccesses,20/20bothstanding,18/20allnon-wristcriteria and nohardwareviolations. Focus on wristfidelity while preserving manipulation. No training/evaluation jobs remain live at restart; resume from retained files. Previous turn classified as progress through completed repeatability evidence and records.

Continuation diagnosis: teacher16 re-collection reproduced all20 physical trajectories exactly. Offline fixed-fingertip IK shows simple linear wrist-to-human interpolation becomes infeasible at several poses; this is not a proof that the criterion is impossible. A planar-only physical reference fit predicts no wrist passes. Next test: offline small rigid hand-and-object frame rotations and horizontal path corrections, constrained by exact table clearance and original object tilt/phase ordering. Relative grasp geometry is preserved in the geometric proposal; inertia/contact changes still require physical PPO rollouts. This is a reference controller retargeting, not post-hoc metric alignment or runtime planning. The final residual network remains PPO-trained, the zero-network base will be reported separately, criteria1/hardware unchanged.

reward_terms.name: opposed_contact
reward_terms.formula: Active:0.6 positional opposition else0.1 any hand;0.8 balanced force/0.6N with opposed normals;0.4exp(-pad-bodySDF^2/.02^2) each thumb/index/middle. Before supported upright left, add0.8*clip(min(three normal forces)/.3N)*clip(norm(cross(index-thumb,middle-thumb))/.0004m2), with opposition and three contacts. Once supported upright left, replace accumulated contact term by0.15*term-0.6*sum(three normal forces)+0.4 anyhand before release-due or-0.4 anyhand after. Always subtract0.15sum min(10,relu(force-4N)). Supported-before-release-due: add max_over_thumb,index,middle exp(-((bodySDF(padskin)-.0015)/.01)^2) to encourage gentle last contact. reward_terms.name: wrist_tracking

Black:.45exp(-position_error²/.055²)+.45exp(-SO3_error²/.45²)-min(4,3(relu(position_error-.08)/.03)²)-min(4,2(relu(SO3_error-1.0471975512)/.3)²). reward_terms.name: opposed_contact
reward_terms.formula: Active:0.6 positional opposition else0.1 any hand;0.8 balanced force/0.6N with opposed normals;0.4exp(-pad-bodySDF^2/.02^2) each thumb/index/middle. Before supported upright left, add0.8*clip(min(three normal forces)/.3N)*clip(norm(cross(index-thumb,middle-thumb))/.0004m2), with opposition and three contacts. Once supported upright left, replace accumulated contact term by0.15*term-0.6*sum(three normal forces)+0.4 anyhand before release-due or-0.4 anyhand after. Always subtract0.15sum min(10,relu(force-4N)). Supported-before-release-due: add max_over_thumb,index,middle exp(-((bodySDF(padskin)-.0015)/.01)^2) to encourage gentle last contact. Release-ready additionally needs phase>=205 white or>=373 black. Release-due requires phase>=205white/373black and span>=3.6white/3.3black, without upper bound. Actual settled/milestone/terminal eligibility retains upper duration bounds through release-ready.

reward_terms.name: lift_height

reward_terms.name: milestones
reward_terms.formula: First settled/release-ready+8; first bottom>1cm+2; one-off-20 for first supporting table contact on right after an upright-air sample. reward_terms.name: action_smoothness
reward_terms.formula: -.02sum(filtered_action²/group_size)-.03sum(action_change²/group_size); legacy29 and extra15 each separately normalized.

reward_terms.name: ordered_rest
reward_terms.formula: Before white first settled:-2min(4,relu(blackXYdrift-.005)/.01); active plug:-2clip((y-.13)/.04,0,1)*relu(blade_tilt-.34906585), no tilt upper cap.

reward_terms.name: terminal
reward_terms.formula: -20000 hardware violation;-25 drop/nonfinite;-100 timeout without stable goal;+20000 both settled/release-ready continuously1.6s AND no hardware/drop/nonfinite and maximum physical penetration<=3mm. Full criteria independently checked.

body.text: Final continuation verdict: PASS, 18/20 trials meet every criterion. Hardware violations: 0/20. Verification r0238; checkpoint research/runs/release_clock_v29_grip_prefix02/final.pt, SHA256 46d3887c3892…; simulation 29. What worked: retained PPO experts, a reconstruction-guided wrist reference, freezing the white expert, and further PPO updates to the black expert. A rigid transform of the grasp reference improved wrist resemblance while preserving relative finger/object geometry. Selected training learning rate: 1e-06; additional airborne contact-loss penalty: 40.0 per 50 Hz training step. Contacts enter this reward only. What failed: changing wrist tilt before the table-assisted turn disrupted that turn; the fixed planar shift in simulation28 also harmed grasp and wrist fidelity. Limitations: uncertain monocular depth, estimated rigid contact physics, allowed oracle object states, and twenty scene-specific seeds reused during diagnosis. This is an own-simulation claim, with no real-robot or broad-generalization claim. Next: independent seeds, friction/inertia sensitivity, object-state estimation and hardware validation. Criteria1 and the retained original16 checkpoint are unchanged. Operator extension r0164 set the hard deadline to 2026-11-05T14:24:56Z; stopping reason: criteria-pass. Remaining failed trials: [{"episode": 1, "failed_checks": ["plug_black_physical_grasp"]}, {"episode": 3, "failed_checks": ["global_phase_order", "wrist_similarity", "plug_black_physical_grasp", "plug_black_transport", "plug_black_final_standing", "plug_black_ordered_phases", "plug_black_grasp_duration"]}]. Simulation29 removed the obsolete white phase205 pause and retained the skipped time in policy clock inputs. Actual evidence time and the fixed phase-normalized wrist comparison were unchanged.

Stage 1 began at 2026-11-02T21:54:44Z with a 60-minute deadline. Reconstruct the actual right hand using HaWoR then the supplied MANO fitter. Treat longitudinal pen roll as unobservable; distinguish video evidence from the four-half-turn sequence specified by TASK.md. No training simulation has been built.

The baseline reconstruction has pen-mask IoU 0.803 and hand precision 0.826, but FCL reports distal finger intersections on 81.7% of frames. Image agreement is insufficient. Refining a writable workspace copy of the supplied fitter with an explicit distal capsule separation term; default fit and all failed checks are preserved.

body.text: Simulation v1 is now recorded as r0006. Its first upload failed because .gz attachments are unsupported, and its next upload lacked the required reconstruction_version field. An inadvertently launched trainer ran 129024 hold-curriculum steps before I noticed; it was interrupted, preserved under research/aborted_before_sim_record, and will not be resumed or evaluated. The new PPO run starts from fresh seed7 weights after r0006. Assets are attached as a genuine NumPy archive of named byte arrays, not a renamed tar file.

Final-policy design: a closed-loop actor/critic network trained with clipped PPO (Schulman et al., https://arxiv.org/abs/1707.06347). The actor sees noisy joint encoders, wrist state, privileged simulated pen pose/velocity, reference targets, previous actions and phase; it outputs 26 bounded residual commands. The retargeted trajectory is an allowed base controller under LEARNING.md, not the reported policy by itself. No execution-time optimizer, pen attachment or object-pose force is used. Criteria v2 additionally requires pair dominance to exclude a constant multi-finger cage.

Iteration1 training return and survival improve, but accepted pair stages remain zero in the running curves. Two likely causes need testing: wrist exploration is too large for 500Hz impedance control, and the initial robot-specific grasp correction decays before the demonstrated first transfer. Next candidate: smaller wrist action variance and retain the initial correction through the first hold, then taper it during transfer. These are hypotheses, not verified task progress.

Start time: 2026-11-04 21:01:58 UTC (date -u at first action; first message immediately preceded it). Hard deadline: 2026-11-05 05:01:58 UTC, with final records reserved before that time. Beginning the mandatory 60-minute reference reconstruction stage; no training simulation will be built before 2026-11-04 22:01:58 UTC and a reconstruction record. I will derive strict ordered pen-spin criteria from the video and instruction, then use PPO and report only evidence-supported simulation results.

Elapsed ~7 minutes. Scene analysis identifies four clockwise turns and the instructed long-finger transfer order, with no thumb grasp and no floor contact. SAM3 with a white-pen box prompt captures the pen but adds shadow fragments; robust line filtering removes these. The initial default MANO fit has hand-mask IoU 0.813 but only 11% near-object contact because its absolute depth is inconsistent with the pen. Next: refit against the corrected whole-pen track, permit hand-to-scene scale adjustment, and resolve foreshortening using hand contact evidence. Pen axial roll and absolute focal/depth are unobservable; they will remain explicitly labelled.

Elapsed ~16 minutes. SAM2.1 video tracking with visually checked endpoint prompts removed shadow artefacts. Directed image-plane rotation is 711.8 degrees over 6 seconds, with nominal half-turn endpoints near frames 48, 88, 151 and 174. Wrist landmark-frame orientation varies by about 30 degrees and reconstructed wrist displacement spans about 9 cm; metric depth and gravity remain monocular estimates. A workspace-only extension of the MANO fitter adds the task long-finger pair contacts and distal-finger clearance; the installed tool remains unchanged. Preliminary reference checks expose shallow adjacent-finger intersections, so refinement continues rather than accepting silhouette overlap as physical correctness.

body.text: First reconstruction recorded as r0004 (version 1) at 21:20:48 UTC. check_reference.py reports VALID with 0 errors and 0 warnings; validate_reconstruction.py overall passes, with the expected thumb-opposition warning for long-finger pen passing. Pen replay median IoU is 0.831; all 180 right-hand frames remain valid and finger self-intersection count is zero. This is a kinematic reconstruction, not evidence of robot policy success. Stage 1 continues to 22:01:58 UTC; remaining effort targets uncertainty, precise pair-contact identity, timing and wrist-pose evidence. No training simulation has been built.

At ~31 minutes, reference version 1 remains preserved and VALID. Further inspection found fingertip errors hidden by high whole-hand IoU. I added 48 manually estimated visible fingertip points on 13 keyframes, then extra visible anchors and bidirectional image tracking (unsupported tracks are omitted). A refined MANO fit now follows these image measurements with roughly 3 px weighted error and still has no finger intersections. I also optimized pen endpoint depths jointly over time and contact evidence without changing their image rays: median centre correction 1.0 mm, p95 7.3 mm, one uncertain fast-spin frame shifts 35 mm. Version 2 is being validated; reconstruction now also includes Blender-built convex end-profile collisions rather than a uniform barrel-only collision model.

Additional reconstruction diagnostics: manual-tip RMS error drops from 31.6 px in reference v1 to 1.44 px in the candidate, and weighted tracked-tip RMS drops from 29.9 to 2.55 px. Full validation still passes and pen replay IoU improves to 0.846. However, a task-specific check finds that middle-ring surface points are not consistently opposite the pen, despite both fingers being near it; the generic thumb-opposition validator cannot resolve this. Next refinement strengthens stable-hold long-finger opposition using the nearest surface points, without forcing opposed grasps during dynamic transfers.

Added full Blender collision profile and contact/continuity-aware pen depth refinement.

body.text: At ~47 minutes, sensitivity to 8px fingertip annotation noise was tested with three independent refits. Wrist orientation changes are small (max 1.95, 3.70, 3.03 degrees), but position sensitivity is larger (max 5.8, 37.2, 16.9mm); one fit has a worse local minimum (loss 1.03 versus 0.34 nominal). I am attempting recovery with smaller optimization steps and will keep all outcomes. These are local fitting sensitivities, not calibrated bounds on camera/metric-depth uncertainty. Reference v2 stays preserved; its stricter task-specific stable contact checks all pass. The final clipped video does not establish a fully settled hold, so verification will operationalize the instruction’s terminal hold explicitly.

The annotation-noise outlier recovered from loss 1.033 to 0.409 after reducing optimization step sizes. These sensitivity runs do not replace the recorded reconstruction or establish ground truth; monocular camera and depth ambiguities remain. Final reference v2 measures 719.0 degrees clockwise in world heading, wrist displacement up to 10.2cm and wrist orientation range 21.0 degrees. Its last 0.20s is still settling (27.3-degree axis variation, 17.7mm pen-to-wrist motion). The criteria draft therefore uses the explicit instruction to require an additional 0.30s settled terminal hold; this is fixed before policy work and is not inferred as a successful hold already shown by the clipped video.

Sensitivity follow-up: the recovered outlier has wrist-position differences median 3.48mm / p95 19.48mm / max 31.91mm, and orientation differences median 1.29deg / p95 5.14deg / max 11.52deg. Thus the initial three fits’ below-4deg maximum is not a complete bound once local-minimum recovery is included. The criteria draft states both results and retains explicit orientation/depth uncertainty; no sensitivity fit replaces recorded reference v2.

Continuous force feasibility remains unresolved: extra interpolation diagnostic still finds up to7.5mm axis-in-hand depth in other fast-turn intervals. All 180 right-hand frames retained; no finger self-intersections; stable pair checks remain close/opposed.

body.text: The full 60-minute reconstruction stage has ended (start 21:01:58 UTC; boundary 22:01:58 UTC). Three references were recorded; v3/r0012 is selected. The output contract is VALID and the supplied validator passes, but the added midpoint diagnostic reveals residual continuous geometry/force uncertainty up to7.5mm axis-in-hand overlap. This limitation is explicitly retained; the robot simulation must restore physical feasibility under rigid-body contacts. No robot training simulation or policy training was built during Stage 1. I now freeze reconstruction and proceed to the prewritten strict criteria, then simulation and PPO.

The first dynamic reference-controller baseline retains the pen for about6.3s but violates finger speed limits at35 physics ticks and does not establish task completion. Initial native-mesh checks show up to6.6mm intersections between inactive robot fingers after human-to-robot retargeting; the larger robot phalanges cannot simply copy hidden human finger positions. I am refining the offline kinematic reference with native mesh-distance constraints and spread priors for inactive fingers, while preserving wrist mapping, hardware parameters and object dynamics. This reference controller is an analysis/baseline; the reported policy will require closed-loop PPO and comparison against this baseline.

body.text: Protocol deviation and correction: the first simulation upload was rejected because scene attachments do not accept ZIP. A shell sequencing error then started a short PPO job before successful simulation recording. I stopped that job, retained its logs/curves as aborted_before_sim_record, and will not use its weights or claim it as a valid evaluated iteration. Simulation version1 is now accepted as r0016, with legitimate uint8 NPZ asset packaging and JSON source text. A fresh PPO run starts only after this accepted simulation record; no checkpoint is carried over.

PPO iteration1 is running in1024 parallel environments on simulation1. Early training has many hardware-speed terminations during stochastic exploration. In parallel I will test iteration2 with smaller wrist residual ranges (15mm,0.15rad versus35mm,0.35rad) and a slower residual filter (new action weight0.1 versus0.2), preserving all physical controllers, geometry and criteria. This should reduce target-velocity noise and wrist-induced finger back-driving while the fingers learn transfers. Both runs use deployable state-only actors and will be separately recorded when evaluated.

body.text: Simulation2 accepted as r0024 before its training. Runs3/4 compare broad orientation reward4*(1-angle/pi), heading-rate match, and smooth minimum-pair force reward: run3 resumes run2 in sim1; run4 starts fresh in sim2. A third concurrent run5 resumes run2 weights in sim2 with larger0.65rad joint residual and more nonzero-phase resets (initial fraction0.3 vs0.6), testing whether wider exploration and transfer initialization help. Each uses PPO only and legal state observations; all20-seed tests retain fixed criteria1. Physical dynamics/robot gains remain identical across simulations; only fixed retarget mapping and reference/reset poses change.

While PPO3/4/5 train, I will use offline CEM trajectory search only as analysis/reference construction, not as an execution-time policy or an RL algorithm. LEARNING.md explicitly allows trajectory optimization for analysis or building a reference; only PPO will train the final closed-loop network. Initial goal is a robust IM grasp over0–1.1s, since v1 controllers squeeze the wrong orientation rather than transfer and sim2 baseline first80ms continuous support occurs too late. Search actions are native PD target residuals; pen remains unactuated. Any optimized reference will be recorded as a new simulation before PPO uses it, and its untrained performance reported separately.

Offline initial-grasp candidate establishes initial IM support by0.136–0.180s in all20 strict perturbation episodes (both1kHz contact ticks), but full baseline remains0/20. First offline turn search reached127deg with MR support; variant2 adds distal joints, angle-gated contact, geometry shaping, and exploration restarts, currently reaching180deg without a catch. Neither is a PPO success. Concurrent PPO run6 branches from a frozen intermediate run4 checkpoint, sim2, 4096environments,200M additional transitions, min2s episodes. New reward adds1.5 pair-centerline proximity and0.3 opposition, -0.2 velocity-margin cost, failure penalty -2 instead of-0.5; GAE lambda0.995. Initial GPU benchmark4096worlds achieved408k simulation-only transitions/s (short nominal hold, not representative training). Every evaluated PPO run will receive iteration+verification records.
